mnemonic_history: The character combines the radical 辶 (walk) and 文 (language/script). Mnemonic: Walking over to point at *this* specific text.
Originally an oracle bone pictogram depicting a saw-toothed weapon or rake. Over time, it was borrowed for the pronoun 'I'. Mnemonic: 'I' hold my weapon to defend myself.
Combines 我 (I/me) with the plural marker 们 (men). 们 uses the person radical (亻) and door (门) for sound. Mnemonic: A group of people (亻) walking through a door (门) together makes 'us'.
Combines the person radical 亻 and 尔 (ěr), which originally meant a loom but was borrowed for sound/meaning. Mnemonic: A *person* (亻) looking directly at *you*.
Combines the person radical 亻 and 也 (yě), meaning 'also'. Mnemonic: That *person* over there is *also* a guy (he).
Combines the female radical 女 (nǚ) and 也 (yě), which means 'also'. Mnemonic: That female (女) is also (也) someone (she/her).
The right side 阝 represents a city or place. Mnemonic: Pointing out a specific place or thing over *there*.
Adds the mouth radical 口 (kǒu) to 那 (that). Mnemonic: Using your mouth to ask *which* one of those things you are talking about.
Combines 哪 (which) and 儿 (suffix). Mnemonic: Asking 'which place' to find out *where* something is.
Contains the speech radical 讠 and 隹 (short-tailed bird). Mnemonic: Trying to figure out *who* is speaking to the bird.
什 originally meant a group of ten, and 么 is a suffix. Mnemonic: Looking at ten people gathered and asking, 'What are they doing?'
A literal combination of 多 (many) and 少 (few). Mnemonic: Is the amount many or few? Asking *how much*.
Originally depicted a small, low table. Mnemonic: Asking *how many* items you can fit onto this small table.
怎 contains the heart radical 心 at the bottom. Mnemonic: Feeling in your heart a sense of wonder about *how* something happened.
Combines 怎么 (how) and 样 (appearance/shape). Mnemonic: Asking *how* that shape or idea looks to you, as in 'how about it?'
A simple pictograph. Mnemonic: A single horizontal line representing the number *one*.
A simple pictograph. Mnemonic: Two horizontal lines representing the number *two*.
A simple pictograph. Mnemonic: Three horizontal lines representing the number *three*.
Looks like a mouth or enclosure 口 with lines inside. Mnemonic: Four curtains drawn inside a square window.
Originally written as criss-crossing lines in ancient Chinese to signify the number five. Mnemonic: Two lines crossing over the top and bottom borders.
Looks like a person with arms outstretched. Mnemonic: A person trying to carry *six* heavy bags at once.
Two lines splitting away from each other. Mnemonic: Dividing something into *eight* pieces.
Looks like a hook or an arm. Mnemonic: Reaching your arm out to grab the *ninth* item.
A vertical line crossing a horizontal line. Mnemonic: A cross pointing in all *ten* directions (including up and down).
Contains the person radical 人 (rén) above a vertical stick 丨 (gǔn). Mnemonic: A single person standing like a stick, representing one individual unit.
Originally composed of elements meaning Jupiter (the year star) and foot (movement). Mnemonic: Counting the passing years to measure age.
A tree 木 (mù) with a line at the bottom indicating the root. Mnemonic: Books are bound at their root (spine) and made from trees.
Combines 此 (this) and 二 (two). Mnemonic: Taking 'these two' steps to gather *some* extra items.
Contains the earth radical 土 (tǔ). Mnemonic: Grabbing a *chunk* or *piece* of solid earth.
An ancient pictogram of a bird flying away toward the sky, later symbolizing negation. Mnemonic: The bird says *no* and flies away.
Contains the water radical 氵 (shuǐ) and a weapon/action radical 殳 (shū). Mnemonic: Dropping your weapon into the water—now you have *no* weapon.
Combines a step 彳 (chì) and tough 艮 (gěn). Mnemonic: Taking a step that is *very* tough to make.
Combines 大 (big) and an extra dot 丶 (diǎn). Mnemonic: It’s already big, but you added a dot—now it's *too* big.
Combines 者 (person/thing) and 阝 (city). Mnemonic: *All* the people gathering in the capital city.
Literally translates to one (一) dot (点) plus the suffix (儿). Mnemonic: Just a single tiny dot, meaning *a little bit*.
